now.title: If they met now
now.intro: Current ratings in each discipline both play, and {a}'s chance of winning against {b}. Singles and men's or women's doubles are only compared between players of the same gender. In doubles, the chance is with equally rated partners: a pair's rating is the average of its players'.
now.introDoubles: Current ratings and pair A's chance of winning against pair B. A pair plays at the average of its players' ratings, and pairs are compared in the discipline their genders put them in: two men's pairs in men's doubles, two mixed pairs in mixed doubles.
now.noChances: {list}, so there are no chances to compare.
now.differentDisciplines: The pairs don't play in the same doubles discipline, so their ratings can't be compared.

fun.title: Just for fun
fun.intro: Men and women are rated in separate disciplines, so their ratings can't be compared as they are. Here are {a}'s and {b}'s chances if they did, with the woman's rating moved onto the men's scale. In doubles, the chance is with equally rated partners.
fun.introDoubles: Pair A is a {kindA} and pair B a {kindB}, so they don't play in the same discipline. Here everyone plays on the men's doubles scale: men at their men's doubles rating, women at their women's doubles rating moved onto the men's scale, and a pair at the average.

genderGap.note: Women's ratings are moved onto the men's scale using the {matches} matches women have played against men in {men}, set against their rating in {women} at the time. A woman rated {w1} plays like a man rated about {m1}, one rated {w2} like one rated about {m2}, and one rated {w3} like one rated about {m3}: the gap grows with the level.
genderGap.extrapolated: Ratings marked * are beyond those the matches cover (about {from} to {to}), so for them the gap is extrapolated.
